theme: The clocks go back, so the usual call time may stop working. Ask your parent what time suits them now, and let the call be easy.

posts.text: The clocks go back soon, and the call time you always use may stop working. Ask your parent what time suits them now. They have been running their own days for a long time.
posts.alt: Three-panel comic. Sam at his desk looks at a wall clock and asks on the phone, 'Is five still a good time?' June, in the garden with gloves and a trowel, answers, 'Make it four. Light goes early.' Sam laughs and writes the new time on a sticky note. Captions: The clocks go back soon. She picked the new time.

posts.title: Ask what time suits them now

script.say: When the clocks change, the time you always call can stop working for someone.
script.broll: Founder to camera, kitchen counter behind him.

script.say: So ask. What time suits you now? They know their own day better than I do.
I built Kettle for the days between calls. It notices a normal morning happened on the phone they already own, and asks them first if it did not.
script.broll: Neutral b-roll: a plain phone face down on a kitchen table, no app visible.

script.say: Then the call can be whenever they like.
script.overlay: The call can be whenever they like

posts.text: Same morning, different light. Your parent's tea is still hot at the same hour, even if your calendar says it got dark early. The call can be about the weather.
posts.alt: Three-panel comic. June sits on a garden bench with a mug, a phone beside her, the green kettle on a small table. Sam on a train with dusk outside says, 'Mine got dark at four.' June laughs on the phone and says, 'Mine too. Tea's still hot.' Captions: Same morning, new light. The call can be about the weather.

posts.title: A call at a time that suits them

script.say: Some calls go better in the morning. Some after tea. Some at the weekend.
script.overlay: Some calls go better after tea
script.broll: Kitchen table, a mug, a phone face down.

script.say: A call goes best when the time is theirs. So I ask what suits them.
Kettle tells us twice a day that a normal morning happened. The call does not have to prove anything.
